query: Unit tests for an Arduino Uno module: Pomodoro timer with TM1637 display, DS1307 statistics and a single button. Pins: pin 3 OUTPUT TM1637 CLK; pin 4 OUTPUT TM1637 DIO; pin 6 INPUT button (HIGH = pressed, external pull-down); pin 9 OUTPUT buzzer (tone); pin 18 I2C DS1307 SDA (A4); pin 19 I2C DS1307 SCL (A5). Arduino API used: attachInterrupt, delay, digitalRead, noTone, pinMode, sizeof, tone. Libraries: Rtc by Makuna, Grove 4-Digit Display, TimerOne. Library API used: Begin, Copyright, Day, DayOfWeek, GetDateTime, GetIsRunning, GetMemory, IsDateTimeValid, LastError, Minute, Month, RtcDateTime, Second, SetDateTime, SetIsRunning, SetMemory, SetSquareWavePin, Year, attachInterrupt, clearDisplay, countof, delay, digitalRead, display, displayNum, displayStr, for, init, initialize, pinMode, point, return, set, sizeof, switch, uint8_t. Simulated devices: wokwi-ds1307, wokwi-tm1637-7segment, wokwi-pushbutton, wokwi-buzzer. wokwi-tm1637-7segment (Wokwi simulator part) / Using the 7-segment display

## Using the 7-segment display

This variant of the seven segment display uses the TM1637 chip. You'll only need 2 microcontroller pins to communicate with it.

The module comes in two forms: one with a colon between the second and third digits (common on clock modules), and one with a decimal point after each digit. Set the `type` attribute to "dp" for the decimal point module. Bit 7 (the DP segment) of a digit byte lights the colon on the colon module, and that digit's decimal point on the "dp" module.

The TM1637 communication protocol is non-standard. It resembles the I2C protocol, but it is simpler and incompatible with I2C. Luckily, you can use a library and not worry about the implementation of the protocol. Here are some TM1637 libraries you can use on Arduino: RT1637_RT(https://github.com/RobTillaart/TM1637_RT), Grove 4-Digit Display.
